Subject: Transition plan & kickoff: Solarflare (Redwood Dedicated)

Hi team,

Thanks again to Alex and the Solarflare crew for a smooth procurement cycle — PO received and countersigned. Attaching the PO and the implementation scope we reviewed. Quick handoff note so CS/Platform can pick up execution: 

Summary: Solarflare (network security SaaS) purchased a Redwood Dedicated pool for production inference (3 x A100 equivalent) with a go-live target of 2026-03-15. The initial use case is conversational support triage + reranking of KB results.

Key commitments / timeline:
- Hardware & infra provisioning: target completion 2026-03-01
- SSO + provisioning + SFTP ingest: 2026-03-08
- End-to-end validation & load test: 2026-03-12
- Go-live: 2026-03-15

Initial success metrics (from sales):
- 95th percentile p99 latency <= 350ms for 128 token responses
- Cost per 1k tokens within agreed band in the SOW
- Accuracy improvement on triage flows measured by rerank P@3 + labeled evals

Known constraints / blockers:
- Solarflare requires customer-managed KMS for keys (they have an HSM vendor; contact: it@solarflare.io)
- They will route traffic through a private VPC peer; network team needs the exact IP ranges by EOD 2026-02-20
- Data retention policy: logs retained 90 days; audit logs must be exportable for SOC2 review

Attachments: Solarflare_PO_0426.pdf, implementation_scope.xlsx [stubs] 

Asking CS: please take lead on kickoff, own the MAP (mutual action plan), and assign a primary CSM. I've looped in Marissa as the first choice; Sean for any escalation and Dev for infra handoffs. Alex — feel free to add or correct anything I missed.

Next step: Marissa, can you confirm owner and propose a 60-min kickoff slot next week that includes: Redwood Platform eng (infra), Solarflare infra, and product owner?

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

1) SLA/uptime expectations in the contract: is Solarflare purchasing the standard Dedicated SLA (99.9%) or the enterprise SLA?
